title: Supreme Court asks Centre to consider a law or awareness on health risks of consanguineous marriages; NFHS-5 puts Tamil Nadu highest at 28%
headline: Tamil Nadu: 28% of Married Women Wed Relatives. Top Court Seeks Centre's View

fact_sources.fact: 20 Nov 2026: bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued a limited notice to the Centre; regulating marriage customs is Parliament's domain; not directing the government to legislate; Centre to consider a law or awareness incl. school/college curricula
Petitioner: 20-year-old law student whose parents are first cousins; 40% visual impairment (counsel/plea)
Plea asks for (mandatory) premarital genetic counselling in high-prevalence areas, voluntary screening, a nationwide awareness campaign; existing marriages not to be criminalised
NFHS-5 (2019-21): Tamil Nadu 28% (highest), Karnataka 27%, India about 11% (10.8%) of ever-married women aged 15-49 married to a blood relative
